findings.statement: Gross margin was higher year over year in the second quarter and first half of fiscal 2027, which the filing attributes to improved mix from Blackwell Ultra.
findings.rationale: The filing states the year-over-year increase and gives a business reason (mix), not only the lapping of a charge. The comparison is against a depressed first half of fiscal 2026, so it shows recovery more than a clear upward trend.

quotes.text: Gross margin increased to 75.0% for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 compared to 72.4% for the second quarter of fiscal year 2026, and 75.0% for the first half of fiscal year 2027 compared to 66.6% for the first half of fiscal year 2026 due to improved mix from Blackwell Ultra.

findings.statement: Sequentially, gross margin is not expanding: the filing calls it approximately flat, and the reported quarterly figures sit at 75.0%, 74.9% and 75.0%.
findings.rationale: The company itself describes the latest quarter as approximately flat sequentially, and the three most recent quarterly figures are essentially the same, which does not show ongoing expansion.

quotes.text: Gross margin increased from a year ago on improved mix from Blackwell Ultra. Gross margin was approximately flat sequentially as our Blackwell architecture remains the vast majority of our revenue.

findings.statement: The first-quarter fiscal 2027 increase to 74.9% from 60.5% is attributed mainly to the prior year's $4.5 billion H20 charge, not to underlying expansion.
findings.rationale: The filing says the year-over-year jump is primarily a base effect from a one-time charge, so it should not be read as evidence of an expanding trend.

quotes.text: Gross margin increased to 74.9% for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 compared to 60.5% for the first quarter of fiscal year 2026, primarily due to the prior year's $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations.

findings.statement: On a full-year basis gross margin fell, to 71.1% in fiscal 2026 from 75.0% in fiscal 2025.
findings.rationale: The most recent complete fiscal year shows a decline, attributed to the product transition and the H20 charge. Expansion since then is a recovery to the earlier level rather than a new high.

quotes.text: Gross margins decreased to 71.1% in fiscal year 2026 from 75.0% in fiscal year 2025 as our business model transitioned from offering Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions and a $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026.

response.rationale: The evidence is mixed and depends on the comparison period. Year over year, gross margin is higher in fiscal 2027 quarters, but much of that is recovery from the depressed fiscal 2026 base. Sequentially it is approximately flat at about 75%, and the last full fiscal year showed a decline. The claim of expansion is supported only for the year-over-year view and is not supported as an ongoing upward trend.
unknowns: Whether gross margin will rise, hold or fall in the next quarter, which is what matters for the earnings decision.
How much of the margin level depends on Blackwell Ultra mix and whether that mix can improve further.
How future inventory provisions or purchase-obligation charges might affect margin.
Any company guidance for gross margin, which is not in the supplied passages.
